put.description: Raw body (optionally gzip), at most the configured artifact limit. The client chooses the id (`art_<ULID>`), so retries are idempotent: the same id and content returns `200`, different content `409`. `X-Content-SHA256` (hex) is verified against the body as sent. Needs a project-bound key with `artifacts:write`. The server redacts before storing (ADR-130): secret-shaped text is replaced with `[REDACTED:...]`, and in a project whose capture mode is METADATA_ONLY or DISABLED, or when the body is too large or fails to scan, the artifact is created with a one-line note in place of the body. The returned `sha256` and `size_bytes` describe what is stored, so they can differ from the upload. A retry of a stored upload is a duplicate whatever the project's mode is now.

get.description: Computed on read from derived data; nothing is stored. Steps are aligned by what the agent did, with ids, timestamps and temporary paths normalised, and the first divergence and the first outcome difference are reported. Without `payload.read` the alignment uses tool, model and span kinds only (`alignment: metadata`), every relation is computed from that projection, and files are per-side counts. Runs longer than the event or step caps are cut and flagged; a middle too different to align within the work budget is reported as unaligned blocks (`alignment_quality: partial`). Comparing a run with itself is allowed.

get.description:
Live events of one run as Server-Sent Events.

Messages: `event: trace_event` (`id:` is the event id, `data:` an event without payload, as in
the list endpoint), `event: run_end` (the run finished and nothing arrived for a while: do not
reconnect) and `event: error` (reconnect). `: keepalive` comments keep idle connections open. The
server closes a stream after its maximum lifetime; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`.

Resume with the `Last-Event-ID` header (browsers send it on reconnect) or `last_event_id` for the
first connection. The server re-sends a short window of events already seen: de-duplicate by event
id. Without either, the stream starts at the beginning of the run. Payloads are never streamed.

The credential is re-checked while the stream is open (every `ABB_STREAM_REAUTH_SECONDS`, default
30): a revoked or expired key or session, a removed member, or a role without run access ends the
stream with `event: error` (`STREAM_UNAUTHORIZED`, not retryable). Reconnecting then gives the
precise 401, 403 or 404. Open streams are limited per key, and per person across tabs and devices.
